hero.headline: Kimi Antonelli overtakes Lewis Hamilton to win British Grand Prix sprint race
hero.teaser: Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli claimed victory in the sprint race at the British Grand Prix, passing teammate Lewis Hamilton on the Hangar Straight during an action-packed contest
hero.body:
Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli claimed victory in the sprint race at the British Grand Prix, passing teammate Lewis Hamilton on the Hangar Straight during an action-packed contest at Silverstone.

Hamilton started from pole position and led for the opening half of the 17-lap sprint, maintaining a one-second advantage over Antonelli as the pair opened a five-second gap on their competitors. However, Antonelli's superior pace allowed him to close the gap steadily. By lap seven, he was within three-tenths of a second, and on lap nine he swept past Hamilton to take the lead.

The Italian driver then extended his advantage ruthlessly, crossing the line with a two-and-a-half-second lead to secure his first Formula 1 sprint victory. Hamilton held on for second place in a hard-fought effort, despite being unable to match the speed of his teammate's Mercedes.

Lando Norris claimed third for McLaren after a frenetic battle involving George Russell and Max Verstappen. Russell, who started fifth, moved up to fourth after exploiting Mercedes' power advantage to pass Verstappen on lap ten. Norris had shown strong pace during the sprint, briefly taking Antonelli's position before the Italian reclaimed it on the same lap.

The result extends Antonelli's advantage in the championship standings, leading Russell by 43 points and Hamilton by 47 points. This marks another impressive performance from the second-year driver, who had been narrowly beaten to pole by Hamilton but demonstrated great determination over the sprint distance.

Hamilton will find some encouragement in Ferrari's competitive showing throughout the weekend. Despite the disappointment of losing the sprint to his teammate, the seven-time world champion fought hard to secure second place in front of his home crowd. His resilience and tactical driving earned him credit despite the power deficit that ultimately proved decisive.

The sprint format, which awards points to top finishers and determines part of the starting grid for Sunday's main race, has set up an intriguing dynamic within the Mercedes team. Both drivers will start near the front of the grid for the feature event, with the sprint performance confirming that Mercedes possesses strong pace at their home circuit.

Antonelli's victory suggests he will carry momentum into the main Grand Prix, while Hamilton has the opportunity to respond in the longer race format. The competitive showing from both Mercedes cars at the front of the field indicates the team will play a central role in the weekend's outcome.

cards.headline: Trump envoys to visit Moscow and Kyiv this weekend as U.S. pushes new peace proposal
cards.teaser: U.S. negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will travel to Russia and Ukraine this weekend as part of efforts to broker a peace deal in the war that began with Russia's invasi
cards.body:
U.S. negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will travel to Russia and Ukraine this weekend as part of efforts to broker a peace deal in the war that began with Russia's invasion in February 2022. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed he will meet the envoys on Sunday, following their talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Saturday. President Donald Trump told reporters the envoys are bringing a proposal to end the war, though a gulf remains between the two sides.

Witkoff and Kushner, Trump's son-in-law, have visited Russia multiple times but this will be their first trip to Ukraine since leading the U.S. peace effort. Zelensky said he would guarantee the safety of Russian airspace during the envoys' visit and called for Russia to reciprocate for Ukraine. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov declined to confirm the visit but said the government would inform reporters when such contacts take place.

Putin told an international economic forum on Thursday that there are chances a peace deal could be reached, saying Moscow and Kyiv must first agree between themselves. He showed no sign of backing down from demands that include additional territorial concessions from Ukraine. Kyiv and its European allies have repeatedly rejected Putin's terms, calling them tantamount to capitulation.

Earlier on Friday, Zelensky said a Russian drone struck the Kyiv office of Oleksandr Poklad, head of the SBU security service. Poklad appeared unharmed. Zelensky said he ordered Poklad to respond adequately to the attack. Russia currently controls about 20 percent of Ukrainian territory.

cards.headline: US military strikes three Iranian oil tankers in retaliation for attacks on American warships
cards.teaser: The US military struck three Iranian oil tankers on Saturday in retaliation for attacks on American warships, escalating a six-month conflict that has disrupted global energy suppl
cards.body:
The US military struck three Iranian oil tankers on Saturday in retaliation for attacks on American warships, escalating a six-month conflict that has disrupted global energy suppl

US Central Command said it permanently disabled two tankers, including one near Kharg Island, and completely destroyed a third in the Gulf of Oman. The attacks came after Centcom said it evaded multiple attacks from Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps earlier in the day targeting a US aircraft carrier and guided-missile destroyer.

cards.teaser: Crude oil prices surged past $90 a barrel after a two-month window for negotiations between the United States and Iran expired without progress, triggering renewed military exchang

Crude oil prices surged past $90 a barrel after a two-month window for negotiations between the United States and Iran expired without progress, triggering renewed military exchang

Brent crude rose above $90 for the first time since late July, reaching $91.63 by Tuesday morning. The escalation came after Iran signaled it would adopt a more aggressive military stance if talks failed, while President Donald Trump demanded Tehran "put up the white flag of surrender" in a Fox News interview.

cards.headline: Trump announces deal for U.S. access to Venezuelan oil reserves
cards.teaser: President Trump says the U.S. has struck an agreement to control 65 billion barrels of Venezuelan oil.
cards.body:
President Trump announced Friday that the U.S. has struck a deal to develop Venezuela's oil reserves, with the American government taking a majority stake in the project. Trump characterized the arrangement as beneficial for Americans, pointing to the nation's vast oil deposits.

Energy experts caution against expecting immediate results. Francisco Monaldi, director of the Latin America Energy Program at Rice University, explained that developing Venezuela's reserves requires substantial time and investment, and would not lead to lower gas prices in the near term.

cards.headline: August Jobs Report Shows Strong Hiring, Raising Pressure on Federal Reserve
cards.teaser: U.S. employers added 162,000 jobs in August, marking an uptick after a sluggish summer for the labor market. The unemployment rate remained steady at 4.1 percent, down from its pea
cards.body:
U.S. employers added 162,000 jobs in August, marking an uptick after a sluggish summer for the labor market. The unemployment rate remained steady at 4.1 percent, down from its pea

The unemployment rate remained steady at 4.1 percent, down from its peak of 4.5 percent in November, according to data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics. The August hiring represents a rebound from inconsistent job growth in recent months.

cards.teaser: Government bond yields have climbed to levels unseen in decades across major developed economies, driven by a combination of geopolitical instability, inflation concerns, and mount
cards.body:
Government bond yields have climbed to levels unseen in decades across major developed economies, driven by a combination of geopolitical instability, inflation concerns, and mount

The widespread sell-off has raised borrowing costs for governments globally and sparked debate about the long-term sustainability of public finances. The surge in yields intensified after ceasefire negotiations between the United States and Iran collapsed on Monday night without reaching an agreement.

cards.headline: Anak Krakatau volcano eruption closes six Indonesian airports, cancels hundreds of flights
cards.teaser: Volcanic ash from Sunday's eruption drifted across western Indonesia, forcing airspace closures in Jakarta and other cities.
cards.body:
An eruption at Anak Krakatau volcano in Indonesia's Sunda Strait on Sunday forced the closure of six airports, including Jakarta's Soekarno-Hatta and Halim Perdanakusuma airports, as volcanic ash spread across parts of the capital and Sumatra's Lampung province. The volcano erupted for 30 seconds in the early hours after showing signs of activity since Friday. No casualties or evacuations were reported.

By mid-afternoon, the closures had disrupted 516 flight movements, including 202 at Soekarno-Hatta that affected approximately 22,800 passengers. Indonesia's civil aviation director warned that cascading disruptions could affect aircraft rotations and fleet availability as airlines work to restore operations. Authorities warned people to stay at least two miles from the crater.

cards.headline: Bus crash on Cape Verde's Fogo Island kills at least 25, mostly students
cards.teaser: A bus carrying students plunged into a ravine on the Atlantic island, officials said.
cards.body:
At least 25 people were killed when a bus plunged into a ravine on Fogo Island in Cape Verde, according to officials and media reports. Most of the victims were students.

The bus fell approximately 100 feet into a rocky ravine during what was reported as a field trip. Multiple others were injured in the crash on the Atlantic island nation.

cards.headline: Lavrov calls Western accusations over Leipzig drone incident 'start of real war'
cards.teaser: Russian Foreign Minister warns of escalating tensions as Germany accuses Moscow of responsibility for attempted airport attack.
cards.body:
Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov said Sunday that Western accusations of Moscow's involvement in a drone incident at Germany's Leipzig airport amount to "the start of a real war." Lavrov accused German Chancellor Friedrich Merz of effectively declaring war on Russia through statements about making Germany a leading military power in Europe.

Germany concluded on Sept. 1 that Russia was responsible for an attempted drone attack at Leipzig/Halle Airport last month and ordered the closure of a Russian consulate and cultural center in Berlin. Russia dismissed the accusations as baseless and claimed Berlin planted evidence to frame Moscow.

cards.headline: Residential student hostel collapses in Delhi with dozens feared trapped
cards.teaser: At least one person was killed and six rescued after the five-story building came down in south-west Delhi.
cards.body:
A five-story residential building housing students collapsed in the Satya Niketan neighborhood of south-west Delhi on Sunday, with as many as 50 people feared trapped inside. At least one person was killed and two others were in critical condition, according to local police. Six people were rescued. Many students were in their rooms at the time as there were no lessons on Sunday.

Delhi police said the building, operating as Hostel Daze near Delhi University campus, was under a 100-year lease and that construction work had been underway in the basement. Authorities evacuated an adjacent building as a precaution. Police are searching for the building owner.

cards.headline: Greek air force F-4 Phantom jet crashes at air show near Athens, killing both pilots
cards.teaser: A Greek air force F-4 Phantom jet crashed during an air show at Tanagra air force base north of Athens on Saturday, killing both pilots. The twin-seat aircraft flew into the ground
cards.body:
A Greek air force F-4 Phantom jet crashed during an air show at Tanagra air force base north of Athens on Saturday, killing both pilots. The twin-seat aircraft flew into the ground

The twin-seat aircraft flew into the ground during a low-altitude maneuver just meters above the surface as thousands of spectators watched during the annual Athens Flying Week event. No civilians were injured.

cards.headline: Egyptian court sentences TV presenter and 11 others to death in drug trafficking case
cards.teaser: Sarah Khalifa and 11 defendants convicted after seizure of more than 750kg of narcotics and raw materials.
cards.body:
Sarah Khalifa and 11 defendants convicted after seizure of more than 750kg of narcotics and raw materials.

An Egyptian court sentenced television presenter Sarah Khalifa and 11 other people to death by hanging after convicting them of drug trafficking charges. The defendants were part of a criminal gang that imported ingredients used to make drugs with intent to sell, according to state-owned newspaper al-Ahram.

hero.headline: Judge declares mistrial in Lindsay Clancy case after jury deadlock
hero.teaser: A Massachusetts judge declared a mistrial in the murder case against Lindsay Clancy after jurors said they could not reach a unanimous verdict. Clancy faced three counts of first-d
hero.body:
A Massachusetts judge declared a mistrial in the murder case against Lindsay Clancy after jurors said they could not reach a unanimous verdict. Clancy faced three counts of first-degree murder in the 2023 deaths of her three children. She did not deny killing her children but pleaded not guilty, with her defense lawyers arguing she was suffering from postpartum psychosis and should not be held criminally responsible.

The trial lasted five weeks and drew national attention. Jurors conceded they would not be able to reach unanimous agreement on the charges. The case divided public opinion throughout the proceedings.

Clancy's defense centered on her mental state at the time of the killings. Her lawyers presented postpartum psychosis as the basis for their argument that she should not be held criminally responsible for the deaths. The prosecution had sought convictions on first-degree murder charges.

The mistrial leaves the case unresolved. Prosecutors will determine whether to retry Clancy on the murder charges.

cards.headline: Fetterman calls former staffers 'disgruntled' after report alleges indifference to Senate duties
cards.teaser: Pennsylvania senator disputes Wall Street Journal account citing ex-aides who described him skipping constituent meetings and a police funeral.
cards.body:
Sen. John Fetterman dismissed former aides as "disgruntled staffers" pushing "smears" after the Wall Street Journal published text messages and accounts alleging he routinely skipped constituent meetings and showed indifference to Senate work. The Pennsylvania Democrat, who faces sagging approval ratings and a possible 2028 reelection bid, called the report the "third hit piece" against him and said leaked messages were stripped of context.

Former staffers created an anonymous account threatening further disclosures. Fetterman defended himself in a statement to CNN, calling a text about a children's hospital meeting a "dumb joke" and saying he took steps to honor three slain police officers after skipping their funeral. The Journal also reported he missed a meeting with paralyzed veterans, which Fetterman said occurred because he was sick that morning.

cards.headline: US envoys meet Zelensky in Kyiv after Putin talks in Moscow
cards.teaser: Trump's negotiators held their first visit to Ukraine since Russia's invasion, following a three-hour meeting with Putin.
cards.body:
President Volodymyr Zelensky met with Donald Trump's envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner in Kyiv, their first visit to Ukraine since Russia's full-scale invasion. Witkoff described the discussion as substantive and said the US team felt encouraged. Kushner said Trump instructed them to find a way to end the war and create conditions for durable peace.

The envoys traveled to Kyiv by train after meeting Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Saturday for three hours of talks the Kremlin called frank and constructive. Putin and Zelensky agreed to halt strikes on each other's capitals for three days during the negotiations. Russian and Ukrainian forces continued exchanging strikes overnight despite the talks.

cards.headline: Jamaica to present slavery reparations petition to King Charles
cards.teaser: The Jamaican government will ask the King to refer legal questions about the enslavement of Africans to the country's highest court.
cards.body:
The Jamaican government will deliver a petition to King Charles on Monday seeking a judicial review of slavery's legality, Culture Minister Olivia Grange said. The petition asks the King, who serves as Jamaica's head of state, to refer three questions to the Judicial Committee of the Privy Council: whether the enslavement of Africans in Jamaica was legal under English law, whether it violated international law, and whether Britain has a legal duty to provide redress.

The petition does not demand payment. Grange said the responses will determine next steps. When Britain abolished slavery in 1833, the government paid £20 million to slave owners in compensation, with loans repaid through 2015. Grange will also meet with British Museum officials to discuss returning colonial-era artifacts to Jamaica.

cards.headline: Building collapse in Delhi leaves dozens trapped, one dead
cards.teaser: A five-story residential building housing students collapsed in India's capital on Sunday.
cards.body:
A five-story residential building in Delhi, India collapsed Sunday afternoon, killing at least one person and leaving dozens of students feared trapped inside. Authorities said as many as 50 people were in the building in the Satya Niketan neighborhood when it came down around 1:30 p.m. local time. Six people have been rescued so far, with two in critical condition.

The building, called Hostel Daze and located near Delhi University campus, had ongoing construction work in its basement at the time of the collapse. A shop owner told local media that excavation work to expand the basement may have weakened supporting pillars. Police are searching for the building owner.

cards.headline: FIFA president Infantino to seek re-election in March
cards.teaser: Gianni Infantino will stand for re-election as FIFA president in March 2027, the governing body confirms, following controversy over a scrapped plan to sell stakes in competitions to private investors.
cards.body:
Gianni Infantino will stand for re-election as FIFA president in March 2027, football's world governing body confirmed. Infantino, who has led FIFA since 2016, faces opposition after abandoning a plan to sell stakes in FIFA competitions to private investment firms, which prompted UEFA to threaten a boycott of all FIFA events including the World Cup.

UEFA is working to field a candidate against Infantino, who would serve until 2031 if re-elected. A challenger requires backing from at least 106 of FIFA's 211 member associations. The football associations of England, Scotland, Wales, and the Republic of Ireland have withdrawn their support for Infantino since the investment plan was announced.

cards.headline: Green Party deputy leader linked to rental properties despite party's landlord opposition
cards.teaser: Mothin Ali controls a company that owns two buy-to-let properties in Leeds, though the party says he acts for vulnerable family members.
cards.body:
Mothin Ali, deputy leader of the Green Party, is the sole director of a company that owns two rental properties in Leeds purchased in 2022 and 2025, despite his party's policy to phase out private landlordism. Ali controls MA Holdings, which bought the properties with buy-to-let mortgages, according to records at Companies House.

The Green Party said Ali acted solely for vulnerable family members with caring responsibilities and does not profit from the properties. The party adopted its policy to phase out private rental ownership in October 2025, after the first property was purchased but before the second. Ali supports the policy, a party spokesperson said.

hero.headline: Historical data shows divided Congress under Republican president tied to 7.33% average annual S&P 500 return
hero.teaser: Stock market data spanning nearly a century suggests Republican leadership with split congressional control delivers more modest gains than other configurations.
hero.body:
Historical stock market data shows that the 34 years featuring a Republican president and a divided Congress produced an average annual return of 7.33% for the S&P 500, according to an analysis of nearly a century of market performance. A divided government occurs when one or both houses of Congress are controlled by Democrats while a Republican holds the White House.

While the data indicates more modest returns under this configuration compared to other political arrangements, the average annual return remains decisively positive. The historical record shows no indication that stocks plunge when congressional control is split, and analysts note that the makeup of Congress is rarely responsible for sharp market downturns, which are typically driven by other factors such as margin debt levels and equity valuations.

cards.headline: Trump threatens trade embargoes on deficit countries unless Federal Reserve cuts rates
cards.teaser: President Donald Trump threatened Friday to halt trade with countries running trade deficits with the United States unless the Federal Reserve lowers interest rates, introducing th
cards.body:
President Donald Trump threatened Friday to halt trade with countries running trade deficits with the United States unless the Federal Reserve lowers interest rates, introducing th

Trump posted on Truth Social directing the central bank to lower rates or face potential embargoes, calling such action potentially better than tariffs and urging the Fed Board to get smart. Speaking later to reporters in the Oval Office, he said he was under no obligation to allow trade and repeatedly floated the idea of banning all trade with Canada.

cards.teaser: A new survey of U.S. employers projects that health care costs will surge by an average of 11 percent in 2027, marking the highest rate of increase in decades. Without significant
cards.body:
A new survey of U.S. employers projects that health care costs will surge by an average of 11 percent in 2027, marking the highest rate of increase in decades. Without significant

Without significant changes to benefit structures, companies face mounting pressure to control expenses while maintaining competitive coverage for workers. The anticipated spike reflects the ongoing challenge of health care cost inflation, which has consistently outpaced general price increases across the economy.

hero.headline: German startup Isar Aerospace becomes first private company to launch commercial rocket into orbit from Europe
hero.body:
Isar Aerospace successfully launched its Spectrum rocket into orbit Saturday from a spaceport in northern Norway, becoming the first fully commercial launch vehicle in Europe to reach orbit. The 92-foot-tall rocket lifted off at 4:12 pm EST from Andøya Spaceport inside the Arctic Circle and reached orbit seven minutes later, carrying five small satellites and a technology experiment.

Founded in 2018 by three students at the Technical University of Munich, Isar raised roughly $1 billion through private financing over eight years and now employs nearly 500 people. The company's CEO, Daniel Metzler, said the launch opens sovereign access to space for Europe and provides an alternative to relying on foreign launch providers. The success marks the largest German rocket in history and the first built predominantly in Germany to reach orbit.

The launch holds geopolitical significance as European governments seek strategic autonomy in space amid difficult relations with the United States. Europe currently must either pay a premium to launch satellites on European rockets or turn to SpaceX, which is politically unpalatable for some officials. The Spectrum rocket can place up to one metric ton of payload into low-Earth orbit, filling a gap between smaller launchers and Europe's heavier Vega-C rocket.

Saturday's flight followed a failed first test in March 2025, when the rocket spun out of control and crashed less than 20 seconds after liftoff due to a vent valve malfunction. The European Space Agency awarded Isar $230 million last month through its European Launcher Challenge program, which aims to foster commercial competition in Europe's launch market. Several other European startups are targeting orbital launch attempts by the end of the year, but Isar now leads the field after demonstrating its capability.

cards.headline: Study links Mars's red color to water-formed iron mineral
cards.teaser: Ferrihydrite, which typically forms in cool liquid water, appears to dominate the planet's dust.
cards.body:
A 2025 study published in Nature Communications identifies ferrihydrite as the likely dominant source of Mars's red color. The poorly crystalline iron mineral contains water in its structure and commonly forms rapidly in cool liquid water on Earth. Researchers matched laboratory spectra of ferrihydrite-basalt mixtures to observations from multiple Mars orbiters and rovers.

The findings suggest Mars acquired much of its characteristic color through chemical weathering while water still flowed across its ancient surface, not solely through dry oxidation after becoming a desert. Ferrihydrite appears stable under current Martian conditions, allowing material formed billions of years ago to persist and spread globally as dust.

cards.headline: Carnegie Mellon researchers demonstrate in-plane Hall effect, breaking 147-year assumption about magnetic field orientation
cards.teaser: Scientists show the Hall effect can work with magnetic fields lying within a material's plane, not just perpendicular to it.
cards.body:
Researchers at Carnegie Mellon University have demonstrated an in-plane version of the Hall effect, in which a magnetic field lying within a material's plane produces a measurable electrical response. The discovery, published in Nature Materials, challenges the conventional understanding of the phenomenon Edwin Hall identified in 1879, which required a perpendicular magnetic field to deflect moving charges and create voltage across a material.

The team layered tantalum iridium telluride with chromium germanium telluride to create an atomically thin device with the symmetry needed to produce the unconventional signal. The researchers said the approach could enable single sensors capable of detecting magnetic fields along multiple directions, with potential applications in electronics, transportation, and medical imaging.

cards.headline: Plug-in solar systems gain legal ground in over a dozen US states
cards.teaser: Appliance-style solar kits that plug into wall outlets are now legal in Virginia, Maine, Colorado, and other states, with California and New York awaiting signatures.
cards.body:
Appliance-style solar kits that plug into wall outlets are now legal in Virginia, Maine, Colorado, and other states, with California and New York awaiting signatures.

More than a dozen US states have passed laws or introduced bills to legalize plug-in solar systems, which allow households to generate electricity using panels and microinverters that connect directly to standard wall outlets. The systems, popular in Europe with an estimated 1.5 million installations in Germany alone, are now legal in Virginia, Maine, Colorado, Maryland, New Jersey, Connecticut, Vermont, New Hampshire, and Utah.

cards.headline: Community tool lets gamers install Nvidia's DLSS 5 on unsupported games and older GPUs
cards.teaser: An unofficial app bypasses manufacturer restrictions to bring neural rendering technology to RTX 20- and 30-series graphics cards.
cards.body:
A community-developed application called DLSS 5 Swapper automates the installation of Nvidia's DLSS 5 neural rendering technology into games that never received official support and extends it to RTX 20-series and RTX 30-series graphics cards, bypassing Nvidia's RTX 50-series requirement. Developer rakanki911 published the tool on GitHub, where it scans for installed games and uses a combination of existing community modifications to enable the feature.

The tool builds on leaked DLSS 5 files from NBA 2K27's pre-launch build that modders have adapted over recent weeks. The application bundles scattered community work into a single interface and reportedly functions across games using DirectX 9 through DirectX 12, as well as select emulators.

cards.headline: Scientists estimate 5.5 million wild bees nesting at New York cemetery
cards.teaser: Researchers documented one of the largest known aggregations of solitary mining bees using emergence traps across 1.5 acres.
cards.body:
Scientists estimate between three million and eight million wild solitary mining bees are nesting underground at a New York cemetery, with 5.5 million as the midpoint, according to research published in the journal Apidologie. Researchers used mesh emergence traps across the 1.5-acre site during spring 2023, capturing 3,251 individual insects and scaling density measurements to calculate the population.

Lead author Steve Hoge and co-authors describe the aggregation as among the largest such concentrations documented in scientific literature. The traps, which ran from late March to mid-May, caught 16 species of bees, flies, and beetles, with mining bees dominating.

cards.headline: The Blood of Dawnwalker sells 1 million copies in three days
cards.teaser: The action RPG from a studio formed by former Witcher developers reached the sales milestone over its opening weekend.
cards.body:
The Blood of Dawnwalker sold more than 1 million copies worldwide in its first three days following release, developer Rebel Wolves announced over the weekend. The studio, formed by former developers of The Witcher series, thanked players for their support. The game reached 70,692 concurrent players on Steam.

Rebel Wolves confirmed it will add a performance mode for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S on launch day after initially indicating the console versions would not support 60 frames per second at release. The studio said player feedback prompted additional testing that gave confidence to include the mode.

hero.headline: Kimi Antonelli overtakes Lewis Hamilton to win British Grand Prix sprint race
hero.teaser: Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli claimed victory in the sprint race at the British Grand Prix, passing teammate Lewis Hamilton on the Hangar Straight during an action-packed contest
hero.body:
Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli claimed victory in the sprint race at the British Grand Prix, passing teammate Lewis Hamilton on the Hangar Straight during an action-packed contest at Silverstone.

Hamilton started from pole position and led for the opening half of the 17-lap sprint, maintaining a one-second advantage over Antonelli as the pair opened a five-second gap on their competitors. However, Antonelli's superior pace allowed him to close the gap steadily. By lap seven, he was within three-tenths of a second, and on lap nine he swept past Hamilton to take the lead.

The Italian driver then extended his advantage ruthlessly, crossing the line with a two-and-a-half-second lead to secure his first Formula 1 sprint victory. Hamilton held on for second place in a hard-fought effort, despite being unable to match the speed of his teammate's Mercedes.

Lando Norris claimed third for McLaren after a frenetic battle involving George Russell and Max Verstappen. Russell, who started fifth, moved up to fourth after exploiting Mercedes' power advantage to pass Verstappen on lap ten. Norris had shown strong pace during the sprint, briefly taking Antonelli's position before the Italian reclaimed it on the same lap.

The result extends Antonelli's advantage in the championship standings, leading Russell by 43 points and Hamilton by 47 points. This marks another impressive performance from the second-year driver, who had been narrowly beaten to pole by Hamilton but demonstrated great determination over the sprint distance.

Hamilton will find some encouragement in Ferrari's competitive showing throughout the weekend. Despite the disappointment of losing the sprint to his teammate, the seven-time world champion fought hard to secure second place in front of his home crowd. His resilience and tactical driving earned him credit despite the power deficit that ultimately proved decisive.

The sprint format, which awards points to top finishers and determines part of the starting grid for Sunday's main race, has set up an intriguing dynamic within the Mercedes team. Both drivers will start near the front of the grid for the feature event, with the sprint performance confirming that Mercedes possesses strong pace at their home circuit.

Antonelli's victory suggests he will carry momentum into the main Grand Prix, while Hamilton has the opportunity to respond in the longer race format. The competitive showing from both Mercedes cars at the front of the field indicates the team will play a central role in the weekend's outcome.

cards.headline: FIFA president Infantino to seek re-election in March amid UEFA opposition
cards.teaser: Gianni Infantino will stand for re-election despite pressure over his scrapped plan to sell stakes in FIFA competitions to private investors.
cards.body:
FIFA president Gianni Infantino will stand for re-election in March, the governing body confirmed Sunday. Infantino, who has led FIFA since 2016, faces opposition after abandoning a plan to sell stakes in FIFA competitions to private investment firms, which sparked threats from UEFA to boycott FIFA events including the World Cup.

Several national football associations, including England, Scotland, Wales, and the Republic of Ireland, have withdrawn support for Infantino. UEFA is working to field a challenger, though no candidates have been named. A candidate needs backing from at least 106 of FIFA's 211 member associations. If re-elected, the 56-year-old would serve until 2031.

cards.headline: Red Sox place All-Star center fielder Ceddanne Rafaela on injured list with quad strain
cards.teaser: Boston loses a key player as it holds a Wild Card position with a 78-65 record.
cards.body:
The Boston Red Sox placed center fielder Ceddanne Rafaela on the 10-day injured list retroactive to September 3 with a right quadriceps strain. The team recalled infielder and outfielder Nate Eaton from Triple-A Worcester to fill the roster spot.

Rafaela, 25, leads Boston with 3.9 fWAR this season while batting .282 with 16 home runs and 17 stolen bases in 569 plate appearances. He ranks among the top seven major leaguers in three defensive metrics and won a Gold Glove in center field last season. The Red Sox entered Sunday at 78-65 and in control of a Wild Card spot.

cards.headline: Jamie Vardy signs with Burnley on season-long deal
cards.teaser: The 39-year-old former Leicester and England striker joins the winless Championship side until the end of the season.
cards.body:
Former Leicester City and England striker Jamie Vardy has joined Burnley on a contract through the end of the season. The 39-year-old, who scored 145 Premier League goals for Leicester before departing for Cremonese in 2025, left the Italian club this summer.

Burnley, relegated from the Premier League last season, sit bottom of the Championship after five winless matches under manager Nicky Hayen. Vardy spent 13 years at Leicester after signing from Fleetwood Town in 2012, scoring 200 goals in 500 appearances across all competitions. He earned 26 England caps.

cards.headline: Eilish McColgan wins London Big Half in return from broken toe
cards.teaser: The Scottish distance runner claimed her fourth victory at the half-marathon after a five-month injury layoff.
cards.body:
Eilish McColgan won the London Big Half on Sunday in her first race since breaking her toe during the London Marathon in April. The 35-year-old Scottish runner finished in 1 hour, 10 minutes, 54 seconds, defeating defending champion Jessica Warner-Judd by 1 minute, 19 seconds. McColgan had crossed the finish line at April's marathon in seventh place with blood seeping through her shoe and was forced to miss July's Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.

The victory marked McColgan's fourth win at the event. The British women's half-marathon record holder said she had not run 13 miles in training and credited a month of warm-weather preparation for the comfortable win over the 13.1-mile course.

cards.headline: Tim Wellens wins Tour of Britain as Nils Politt claims final stage
cards.teaser: The Belgian rider extended his lead on the final day, finishing 42 seconds ahead of Britain's Lewis Askey.
cards.body:
Belgium's Tim Wellens won the 2026 Tour of Britain, extending his overall lead to 42 seconds over Great Britain's Lewis Askey on the final stage. Germany's Nils Politt claimed victory on the 156.1-kilometer stage through Earlston after attacking with nine kilometers remaining, earning his first stage win since 2022.

Askey held on to second place overall, with Belgium's Jasper Stuyven finishing 21 seconds behind him in third. Great Britain's Elliot Rowe finished sixth overall, while compatriots Mark Donovan and Ben Wiggins placed ninth and 10th respectively.

cards.headline: Lane Kiffin's LSU debut produces 31-3 halftime rout of Clemson
cards.teaser: The new Tigers coach delivered a dominant performance in his first game, while Dabo Swinney faces mounting questions about his future at Clemson.
cards.body:
Lane Kiffin's debut as LSU head coach featured a commanding 31-3 halftime lead over Clemson in a game attended by congressional leaders and celebrities. Kiffin told ESPN at halftime, "Imagine if we had pro players," referencing recent headlines about a Louisiana court case.

The lopsided result intensified pressure on Clemson head coach Dabo Swinney, who may be coaching his final season if he cannot reverse the program's trajectory. The game highlighted two programs moving in opposite directions, with Clemson unable to match LSU's performance under its new leadership.

hero.headline: Pro wrestler Andy Williams, known as The Butcher in AEW, dies at 48 after collapsing during match in Pennsylvania
hero.body:
Andy Williams, the professional wrestler known as The Butcher who performed in All Elite Wrestling and other promotions, died after suffering a medical emergency during a match in Millvale, Pennsylvania, on Friday night. Williams, 48, collapsed at the end of his match with tag team partner Jesse Guilmette at Enjoy Wrestling at Mr. Smalls Theater. The Allegheny County Medical Examiner's Office confirmed his death on Sunday.

The promotion said doctors on staff administered CPR immediately after Williams collapsed and continued until an ambulance arrived. The show was stopped and attendees were sent home. All Elite Wrestling released a statement calling Williams a trailblazing musician who made a successful transition into professional wrestling and was respected by his peers both in and out of the ring.

Williams began training as a wrestler in the early 2010s and made his debut in 2015. He and Guilmette formed their tag team in 2017, calling themselves The Butcher and The Blade. The pair appeared in multiple promotions including AEW, Ring of Honor, Total Nonstop Action Wrestling, and others.

Before his wrestling career, Williams was a guitarist for the band Every Time I Die from 1998 until the band broke up in 2022. He was also a musician with Atomic Rule.

cards.headline: Barbara Eden withdraws from film festival appearance due to sudden illness
cards.teaser: The 95-year-old actress was scheduled to receive the Cinecon Legacy Award but canceled at the last minute.
cards.body:
Barbara Eden withdrew from an appearance at the Cinecon Classic Film Festival on Saturday due to a sudden illness, according to event organizers. The 95-year-old "I Dream of Jeannie" star had been scheduled to receive the Cinecon Legacy Award at the event.

The festival honored Eden in absentia, with her "All Hands on Deck" co-star Pat Boone accepting the award on her behalf. Organizers said Eden was regretful about the last-minute cancellation. The nature of her illness was not disclosed.

cards.headline: Susan Sarandon says agencies still discourage her hiring over pro-Palestinian advocacy
cards.teaser: The actor told a Venice Film Festival press conference that she has recently lost film roles due to her support for Palestine.
cards.body:
Susan Sarandon said at the Venice Film Festival on Sunday that she has recently lost film roles because of her pro-Palestinian advocacy. The actor said agencies continue telling people not to hire her, though she feels welcome among the general public and internationally.

Sarandon was dropped by her agency UTA in 2023 after comments she made at a pro-Palestinian rally. She said the director of her new film "The Echo Chamber" was warned against working with her but proceeded anyway.

cards.headline: Wim Wenders says he was misquoted on filmmakers and politics, calls artists 'antidote' to political mindset
cards.teaser: The German director addressed controversy from his February Berlinale remarks at a Venice press conference.
cards.body:
Wim Wenders said Sunday at the Venice Film Festival that he was misquoted when his February comments at the Berlin Film Festival ignited controversy. The German director, who served as jury president at the Berlinale, said he had been quoted as saying filmmakers "should stay out of politics," but that he actually said filmmakers work with empathy while politics works without it. "We are the antidote," Wenders said, wearing an "Imagine Peace" shirt.

Wenders' original February remarks prompted author Arundhati Roy to withdraw from the Berlin festival in protest and forced festival director Tricia Tuttle to issue a statement. At Venice, Wenders presented his documentary "From Inside Out — The Architecture of Peter Zumthor."

cards.headline: Lee Chang-dong's 'Possible Love' Explores Class Divide Through Two Married Couples
cards.teaser: The director of 'Burning' returns with a Venice-premiered drama starring Jeon Do-yeon, coming to theaters in October and Netflix in November.
cards.body:
Director Lee Chang-dong premiered his latest film at the Venice Film Festival, a 164-minute drama examining class tensions through two married couples brought together when a wealthy documentarian attempts to film a working-class family affected by a factory strike. Jeon Do-yeon stars as Mi-ok, whose husband lost his job during mass layoffs at a Korean metals company, alongside Cho Yeo-jeong as Ye-ji, the affluent filmmaker inserting herself into their lives.

Netflix will release the film theatrically on October 23 and on its streaming service November 6. The drama uses its film-within-a-film structure to explore labor, dignity, and the barriers wealth creates between people as the couples spend a weekend at a coastal vacation home.

cards.headline: Wim Wenders' 3D Documentary on Architect Peter Zumthor Debuts at Film Festival
cards.teaser: The two-hour film explores the Swiss architect's work, including his design of LACMA's permanent collection building.
cards.body:
Wim Wenders' latest 3D documentary, "From Inside Out – The Architecture of Peter Zumthor," premiered at a film festival, exploring the work of the Swiss architect through a two-hour examination of his buildings and design philosophy. The film traces Zumthor's career from 1980s archival footage through recent projects, emphasizing his focus on light, natural materials, and structures that feel integrated with their surroundings.

The documentary culminates with extended coverage of Zumthor's design for the Los Angeles County Museum of Art's permanent collection building, depicting its planning and completion. The sprawling structure features exposed concrete and an amoebic layout designed to give equal prominence to all artworks. The film was visited by directors including Ava DuVernay and Werner Herzog during production.

cards.headline: Photographer Bob Minkin recalls documenting New York music scene in the 1970s and 1980s
cards.teaser: Minkin captured performances by Bruce Springsteen, Frank Zappa, the Grateful Dead, and dozens of other acts at venues including the Palladium, the Ritz, and Lone Star Cafe.
cards.body:
Photographer Bob Minkin documented hundreds of concerts in New York and surrounding venues from the mid-1970s through the 1980s, capturing performances by Bruce Springsteen, Frank Zappa, Jerry Garcia, the Ramones, and blues artists including Albert Collins and Buddy Guy. Minkin began tracking shows after attending Eric Clapton at Roosevelt Stadium in 1974, later compiling a list that reached into the hundreds.

Minkin photographed performances at venues including the Palladium, the Ritz, Lone Star Cafe, the Bottom Line, and Wollman Rink in Central Park. He described Springsteen's 1978 Palladium show as among the best he witnessed, recalling the musician played with intense energy. Minkin used techniques including slow shutter speeds with flash to capture movement and experimented with zoom lenses during long exposures.

hero.headline: Trump envoys to visit Moscow and Kyiv this weekend as U.S. pushes new peace proposal
hero.teaser: U.S. negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will travel to Russia and Ukraine this weekend as part of efforts to broker a peace deal in the war that began with Russia's invasi
hero.body:
U.S. negotiators Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will travel to Russia and Ukraine this weekend as part of efforts to broker a peace deal in the war that began with Russia's invasion in February 2022. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed he will meet the envoys on Sunday, following their talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on Saturday. President Donald Trump told reporters the envoys are bringing a proposal to end the war, though a gulf remains between the two sides.

Witkoff and Kushner, Trump's son-in-law, have visited Russia multiple times but this will be their first trip to Ukraine since leading the U.S. peace effort. Zelensky said he would guarantee the safety of Russian airspace during the envoys' visit and called for Russia to reciprocate for Ukraine. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov declined to confirm the visit but said the government would inform reporters when such contacts take place.

Putin told an international economic forum on Thursday that there are chances a peace deal could be reached, saying Moscow and Kyiv must first agree between themselves. He showed no sign of backing down from demands that include additional territorial concessions from Ukraine. Kyiv and its European allies have repeatedly rejected Putin's terms, calling them tantamount to capitulation.

Earlier on Friday, Zelensky said a Russian drone struck the Kyiv office of Oleksandr Poklad, head of the SBU security service. Poklad appeared unharmed. Zelensky said he ordered Poklad to respond adequately to the attack. Russia currently controls about 20 percent of Ukrainian territory.

cards.headline: Trump, Vance to headline GOP midterm convention in Dallas next week
cards.teaser: The president will speak both nights while vulnerable House and Senate candidates join the lineup. Senate Majority Leader John Thune is notably absent.
cards.body:
President Donald Trump and Vice President J.D. Vance will headline the Republican Party's Sept. 9-10 midterm convention in Dallas, according to a preliminary speaker list obtained by Axios. Trump will speak both nights, while Vance will deliver a keynote address on the second night. The lineup includes Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., House Speaker Mike Johnson, and Senate Majority Whip John Barrasso.

Senate Majority Leader John Thune, whom Trump has criticized over election security legislation, is not on the list, though organizers say they are still adding names. Vulnerable Senate candidates scheduled to speak include Ohio Sen. Jon Husted, Texas Republican Ken Paxton, and Michigan Republican Mike Rogers. House members from competitive districts, including New York Rep. Mike Lawler, are also on the roster.

cards.headline: Trump envoys meet with Putin in Moscow, plan Ukraine trip amid airstrike pause
cards.teaser: President Trump envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met with Russian President Vladimir Putin at the Kremlin on Saturday and discussed U.S. ideas for ending the war in Ukraine.
cards.body:
President Trump envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met with Russian President Vladimir Putin at the Kremlin on Saturday and discussed U.S. ideas for ending the war in Ukraine.

The three-hour meeting came as both countries agreed to a short pause in airstrikes to allow the envoys to travel to Kyiv on Sunday. Putin told Witkoff and Kushner at the start of the meeting that he has full trust in U.S.

cards.headline: Trump plans to use Qatari plane for Ireland trip despite security concerns
cards.teaser: President Donald Trump will fly to Ireland next week aboard a Boeing 747 gifted by Qatar, despite ongoing security concerns about the aircraft. Plans to take the plane out of servi
cards.body:
President Donald Trump will fly to Ireland next week aboard a Boeing 747 gifted by Qatar, despite ongoing security concerns about the aircraft. Plans to take the plane out of servi

Plans to take the plane out of service for security upgrades have been pushed back to later this fall. The decision to use the Qatari-gifted aircraft for international travel raises questions about the readiness of the plane for presidential use.

cards.headline: Supreme Court rules political parties entitled to lower TV ad rates
cards.teaser: The Supreme Court delivered a significant victory to Republican and Democratic party organizations Friday, ruling that political parties are entitled to discounted television adver
cards.body:
The Supreme Court delivered a significant victory to Republican and Democratic party organizations Friday, ruling that political parties are entitled to discounted television adver

The decision addresses a long-standing dispute over how broadcast stations must price political advertising under federal communications law. Broadcasters are required to offer candidates the lowest unit rate for ad time during the weeks before an election, but questions have persisted about whether this rule applies to party committees that coordinate with campaigns.

cards.headline: Congress delays government funding and Iran war money until after midterms
cards.teaser: Republican lawmakers have voted to postpone major legislative decisions until after the November midterm elections, setting up a crowded agenda for the final weeks of the year. The
cards.body:
Republican lawmakers have voted to postpone major legislative decisions until after the November midterm elections, setting up a crowded agenda for the final weeks of the year. The

The House overwhelmingly passed a bill to temporarily fund the government, pushing the deadline past Election Day and into the lame-duck session. The postponed items include government funding, additional money for the ongoing conflict with Iran, and the extension of expanded surveillance authorities.

cards.headline: Whistleblower warns rushed USPS portal could reject ballots before midterms
cards.teaser: A federal official has warned that a hastily implemented U.S. Postal Service online system connected to President Trump's mail voting order could reject large batches of ballots ah
cards.body:
A federal official has warned that a hastily implemented U.S. Postal Service online system connected to President Trump's mail voting order could reject large batches of ballots ah

The whistleblower claims the USPS is rolling out the portal without sufficient testing or safeguards, creating concerns about potential disruptions to voting access. The online system is being developed in response to Trump's efforts to restrict mail voting.
